Prealgebra · Lesson 5.1

Place Value and Decimals

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Each place-value column is worth ten times the one on its right, and those columns only ever build whole numbers. But a length between 1414 and 1515 has no whole-number name. So keep the columns running to the right, each one worth a tenth of the one before it.

Problem
In 5.835.83 the digit 88 sits in the first place past the decimal point, the tenths place. What is the value of the 88 alone? Write your answer as a fraction abba​.
Show a hint
  • The value of a digit is the digit times the worth of its place. The 8 is sitting in the tenths place, and one single tenth is worth 10−1=11010−1=101​. So you have 8 of those tenths.
  • Take the digit 88 and multiply it by the place value 110101​. That is 8×1108×101​, which stacks 8 copies of one tenth on top of each other. Write the result as a single fraction.
Show the full solution
The 88 sits one step past the point, in the tenths place, and one unit of that place is worth 10−1=11010−1=101​. Eight of those is 8×110=8108×101​=108​​. A digit's value is always the digit times the worth of its place, so the 55 and the 33 do not affect this one.
Problem
In 5.835.83 the digit 33 sits one step right of the tenths place, in the hundredths place. What is the 33 worth all by itself? Write your answer as a fraction a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • The 3 is one step to the right of the tenths place. Stepping right means the place value gets divided by 10 again, so this new place is worth 110101​ of 110101​.
  • One tenth of one tenth is 110×110=1100101​×101​=1001​, which is 10−210−2. The digit there is a 33, so its value is 33 of those, meaning 3×11003×1001​.
Show the full solution
Step one place right from the tenths and the place value divides by 1010 again, so the 33 sits in the hundredths place, worth 110×110=1100101​×101​=1001​. Three of those is 3×1100=3/1003×1001​=3/100​. That is 10−210−2, and it should come out smaller than the 88 tenths next door, since places shrink as you move right.
Problem
Write the decimal with 5 in the ones place, 7 in tenths, nothing in hundredths, and 3 in thousandths as a single decimal.
Show a hint
  • Set up the columns left to right just as they are named. One column for the ones, then the decimal point, then tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. Drop each given digit into its own column and ask what belongs in the hundredths column when the part is 01001000​.
  • The digits in order are 5, then a point, then 7, then 0, then 3. That zero is not optional. It is the placeholder that keeps the 3 sitting in the thousandths column instead of letting it drift left. Read the columns straight across to get the decimal.
Show the full solution
Drop each digit into its own column, left to right. Ones 55, then the point, then tenths 77, hundredths 00, thousandths 33. Reading straight across gives 5.7035.703​. That middle zero is doing real work. Without it you would write 5.735.73, which puts the 33 in the hundredths place, ten times bigger than intended.
Problem
Write 0.270.27 as a single fraction over a power of ten in the form abba​. Use a common denominator of 100100.
Show a hint
  • You have two pieces, 210102​ and 71001007​. To add them you need the same denominator. Which power of ten do both pieces fit into, 1010 or 100100?
  • Rewrite 210102​ over 100100 by multiplying top and bottom by 1010, which gives 2010010020​. Now add the hundredths together, 20100+710010020​+1007​, and keep the denominator the same.
Show the full solution
The 22 is in tenths and the 77 is in hundredths, so 0.27=210+71000.27=102​+1007​. Rewrite the first piece over 100100 as 2010010020​ and add, 20100+7100=2710010020​+1007​=10027​​. Two decimal places always give a denominator of 102=100102=100, with the digits after the point read as the numerator.
Key idea
Decimal place value. A decimal continues place value past the ones place. Each place is one tenth of the place to its left, so each step right is the next negative power of ten, tenths 10−1=11010−1=101​, hundredths 10−2=110010−2=1001​, thousandths 10−3=1100010−3=10001​. The decimal point does not break that pattern. It only marks where the ones place ends. A decimal and a power-of-ten fraction are the same number written two ways, so you convert by reading, never dividing. The last filled place gives the denominator (one place 1010, two places 100100, three places 10001000). The digits after the point, read as one number, give the numerator. So 0.27=271000.27=10027​ and 0.009=910000.009=10009​.
Problem
A jeweller records a mass as 910109​ of a gram. Write it as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • A denominator of 1010 means tenths, and the tenths place is the first slot to the right of the decimal point. So the only digit you need to write past the point is the 99.
  • Put the 99 in the tenths place, just after the point, and write a 00 in the ones place in front so the answer reads 0.90.9 instead of a lonely .9.9.
Show the full solution
A denominator of 1010 means tenths, and tenths is the first place past the point, so the 99 goes there. There are no whole grams, so a 00 fills the ones place, giving 0.90.9​. That leading zero is only there so the answer does not arrive as a bare .9.9 that is easy to misread.
Problem
Are 0.30.3 and 0.300.30 equal as numbers? Answer yes or no.
Show a hint
  • A trailing zero lives in a brand new place to the right. Ask yourself what that place is actually holding. The hundredths place in 0.300.30 holds a 00, so it contributes 01001000​, and adding nothing to a number leaves it alone.
  • Turn each reading into a fraction and see if they match. 0.30.3 means 310103​. For 0.300.30, write 3010010030​ and simplify by dividing top and bottom by 1010 to get 310103​. Same fraction means same number.
Show the full solution
Read each one as a fraction. 0.30.3 is 310103​. In 0.300.30 the 33 is still in tenths and the new 00 sits in hundredths, adding 0100=01000​=0, so 0.30=3100.30=103​ as well. Same fraction, same number, so yesyes​. Tacking on a trailing zero is the same move as multiplying top and bottom by 1010, which never changes a value.
Fun fact
The leading zero in 0.50.5 is not required by math. A lone dot is easy to miss on a page and a bare .5.5 could be read as a whole 55. The zero guards the point.
Key idea
Trailing versus inner zeros. Where a zero sits after the point changes what it does. A zero at the end fills a place with nothing, so 0.5=0.50=0.5000.5=0.50=0.500 and you may add or drop trailing zeros freely to line decimals up. A zero between the point and a nonzero digit takes the place that digit would have used. That moves the digit one column further from the point and makes it ten times smaller, so 0.50.5 and 0.050.05 are not equal.

A whole number has an exact spot on the number line, but 7.47.4 falls between 77 and 88. Zoom in on that gap. Chop it into ten tenths, then chop each tenth into ten hundredths. The same divide-by-ten step that built the columns lets you land on any decimal.

Problem
The unit from 00 to 11 is split into 1010 equal steps. 0.70.7 means seven tenths. Which numbered mark does 0.70.7 land on?
Show a hint
  • The marks are 0.1,0.2,0.30.1,0.2,0.3 and so on. Walk along them one tenth at a time and count how many steps it takes to arrive at 0.70.7.
  • The number 0.70.7 means 77 tenths, that is 7×1107×101​, so it sits 77 one-tenth steps from 00.
Show the full solution
0.70.7 means seven tenths, that is 7×1107×101​, so it sits seven one-tenth steps from 00 and lands on mark 77​. The digit in the tenths place gives the count directly, so you never have to walk the marks.
Problem
Stack 0.70.7 and 0.680.68 with decimal points aligned. Read from left to right one place at a time. Which is larger?
Show a hint
  • Line up the decimal points and look only at the tenths place to start. One number has 77 tenths there, the other has 66 tenths. The hundredths and anything smaller come later and only matter if the tenths tie.
  • The tenths place already disagrees, so that is where it ends. 77 tenths beats 66 tenths, and even the largest possible hundredths digit in 0.680.68 cannot add up to a full extra tenth. So the number with 77 in the tenths place wins.
Show the full solution
Pad 0.70.7 to 0.700.70 so both numbers show the same places, then read from the left. The tenths place has a 77 against a 66, and that first disagreement settles it, so 0.70.7​ is larger. The most a hundredths digit can be worth is 99 hundredths, still less than one whole tenth, so nothing to the right can close a gap opened in the tenths.
Problem
Which number is larger, 0.50.5 or 0.49990.4999? Stack them with points aligned and compare place by place from the left.
Show a hint
  • Write them one above the other with the decimal points aligned, 0.50000.5000 over 0.49990.4999. Now scan left to right and find the first place where the two digits are different. That place, and nothing after it, settles the question.
  • The first differing column is the tenths. There 0.50.5 shows a 55 and 0.49990.4999 shows a 44. Five tenths already beats four tenths, so the larger number is decided before you ever reach those 99s. All three 99s live in the hundredths, thousandths, and ten-thousandths, places far too tiny to add up to a whole extra tenth.
Show the full solution
Pad to the same length and compare 0.50000.5000 with 0.49990.4999 from the left. The tenths place has a 55 against a 44, so 0.50.5​ is larger. Over a common denominator the gap is 500010000−499910000=110000100005000​−100004999​=100001​. Those three 99s buy finer detail, not more size.
Problem
Order 0.40.4, 0.390.39, 0.4010.401, 0.40090.4009, and 0.410.41 from smallest to largest by aligning decimal points. Which number is third in the list?
Show a hint
  • First order them. Line up the decimal points and read the tenths place. Four splits begin with 44 tenths and one with 33 tenths, so the 33-tenths one is smallest. Then pad the rest with trailing zeros to the same length and compare.
  • Padded to four places the four tied splits are 0.4000,0.4010,0.4009,0.41000.4000,0.4010,0.4009,0.4100, so compare 4000,4010,4009,41004000,4010,4009,4100. The full order is 0.39,0.4,0.4009,0.401,0.410.39,0.4,0.4009,0.401,0.41. Pick the one in the middle.
Show the full solution
Only 0.390.39 opens with 33 tenths, so it is the smallest. Pad the other four to 0.4000,0.4010,0.4009,0.41000.4000,0.4010,0.4009,0.4100 and compare them like the whole numbers 4000,4010,4009,41004000,4010,4009,4100. The full order is 0.39,0.4,0.4009,0.401,0.410.39,0.4,0.4009,0.401,0.41, so third is 0.40090.4009​. It shows the most digits yet is not the biggest, because those extra digits sit in the thousandths and ten-thousandths where they are worth almost nothing.
Key idea
Comparing decimals. Line up the decimal points and read place by place from the left, biggest place first. The first place where the digits differ fixes the order, because nothing further right is large enough to change it. The number of digits a decimal shows is how finely it was measured, not how big it is, so 0.90.9 is larger than 0.09990.0999 despite fewer digits.
Problem
Multiplying by 1010 shifts every digit one place left, so the decimal point appears to hop right. Multiplying by 100100 shifts two places. What is 3.7×1003.7×100?
Show a hint
  • Each factor of 1010 shifts every digit one place toward higher value. You have 100100, which is two tens, so that is two places. Watch where the 33 and the 77 land.
  • Holding the point still, multiplying by 100100 makes it appear to move two places to the right. Starting from 3.73.7, one place gives 3737, and a second place gives 370370.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by 100100 shifts every digit two places toward higher value. The 33 goes from ones to hundreds, worth 300300, and the 77 goes from tenths to tens, worth 7070. Together that is 300+70=370300+70=370​. Watching the point instead of the digits gives the same thing, two places right, 3.73.7 to 3737 to 370370.
Problem
A tag should read 4.504.50 dollars but printed 45.045.0 dollars instead, shifting the decimal point one place right. By how many times is the printed price larger than the correct price?
Show a hint
  • Look at where the digit 4 lives in each price. In 4.50 it is in the ones place, worth 4. In 45.0 it is in the tens place, worth 40. Every digit has jumped up exactly one place.
  • When each digit moves one place to the left, its value gets ten times bigger. So the whole price is ten times bigger. You can check by asking what you multiply 4.50 by to reach 45.0.
Show the full solution
In 4.504.50 the 44 is in the ones place, worth 44. In 45.045.0 that same 44 is in the tens place, worth 4040. Every digit moved one place left, so every digit is worth ten times as much and so is the whole price, making the printed tag 1010​ times larger. Moving the point one place right always multiplies by 1010, and 4.50×10=45.04.50×10=45.0 confirms it.
Key idea
Shifting by powers of ten. Every place is worth ten times the one on its right. So making a number ten times bigger moves each digit one column left, and making it ten times smaller moves each digit one column right. Multiplying by 10k10k moves every digit kk places left, and dividing moves them kk places right, one column per factor of ten. People say the point moves, but the point stays where it is and the digits move. Fill any empty place with 00 so each digit lands in its correct column.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Four splits in seconds: Runner A 0.2050.205, B 0.210.21, C 0.20.2, D 0.20490.2049. Ordered smallest to largest, which split is the second smallest?
Show the solution
Pad every split to four places, 0.2000,0.2049,0.2050,0.21000.2000,0.2049,0.2050,0.2100, and read left to right. All four tie at 22 tenths. In the hundredths only 0.21000.2100 has a 11, so it is the largest. The other three split at the thousandths, where the digits are 00, 44, 55. The order is 0.2,0.2049,0.205,0.210.2,0.2049,0.205,0.21, so the second smallest is 0.20490.2049​.
Practice
In 4.364.36, swap the tenths and hundredths digits. What new decimal do you get?
Show the solution
The swap touches only the two digits after the point. The 66 moves into tenths and the 33 moves into hundredths, while the 44 stays where it is, giving 4.634.63​. Swapping changes the number because the tenths place is worth ten times the hundredths place.
Practice
Write 0.0130.013 as a single fraction a/ba/b with a power-of-ten denominator.
Show the solution
The last digit 33 sits in the thousandths place, so the denominator is 1,0001,000, and the digits after the point read as 1313 on top. That gives 13/100013/1000​. The leading zero adds nothing to the numerator, but it does push the 33 out to thousandths, which is what sets the denominator.
Practice
Write 71001007​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
A denominator of 100=102100=102 means hundredths, the second place after the point. Put the 77 there and a 00 in the tenths place to hold it open, giving 0.070.07​. Drop that inner zero and you get 0.70.7, which is ten times too big.
Practice
A cartridge holds 100100 drops, each weighing 0.3060.306 grams. What is the total weight in grams? Compute 0.306×1000.306×100.
Show the solution
Multiplying by 100100 slides every digit two columns left. The 33 runs from tenths to ones to tens, worth 3030, and the 66 runs from thousandths to hundredths to tenths, worth 0.60.6. Adding gives 30.630.6​ grams. Each factor of ten is one slide, so 100100 is two.
Practice
A weather station records 8.28.2 mm of rain, then converts to meters by dividing by 1,0001,000. What is the rainfall in meters?
Show the solution
Dividing by 1,000=1031,000=103 slides every digit three columns right. The 88 runs from ones down to thousandths and the 22 lands in ten-thousandths, with zeros filling the empty tenths and hundredths. So 8.2÷1,000=0.00828.2÷1,000=0.0082​. Shrinking by a factor of a thousand should land far below 11, and it does.
Practice
A point on the number line is at 14.714.7. What is the smaller of the two whole numbers it sits between?
Show the solution
14.714.7 is 1414 whole units plus 77 tenths, so it sits past 1414 but short of 1515. The smaller of the two is 1414​. The digits left of the point always name the largest whole number the value has fully reached.
Practice
The value 0.730.73 falls between two neighboring tenths. Which of those two tenths is the larger one?
Show the solution
The tenths digit of 0.730.73 is 77, and the 33 hundredths carries it just past 0.70.7. It is 7373 hundredths, still short of the 8080 hundredths that make 0.80.8, so it lies between 0.70.7 and 0.80.8 and the larger tenth is 0.80.8​.
Practice
Which number is larger, 0.60.6 or 0.59990.5999?
Show the solution
Pad the short one to 0.60000.6000 and compare with 0.59990.5999 from the left. The tenths place has a 66 against a 55, so 0.60.6​ is larger. More digits does not mean more value. As fractions, 600010000100006000​ beats 599910000100005999​ by a single ten-thousandth.
Practice
Which number is larger, 0.070.07 or 0.70.7?
Show the solution
In 0.70.7 the 77 is in the tenths place, worth 710107​. In 0.070.07 the zero takes the tenths place and pushes the 77 out to hundredths, worth 71001007​. Since 710=70100107​=10070​, the larger number is 0.70.7​, ten times as big. An inner zero moves a digit, so it changes the value.
Practice
Four forms: 0.60.6, 0.600.60, 0.6000.600, and 0.060.06. How many of these name the exact same amount as 0.60.6?
Show the solution
0.60.6 is 610106​. Then 0.60=60100=6100.60=10060​=106​ and 0.600=6001000=6100.600=1000600​=106​, so counting 0.60.6 itself that is 33​ forms naming the same amount. 0.060.06 is the odd one out, since its zero sits before the 66 and drops it to hundredths, ten times smaller.
Practice
A receipt should read 8.308.30 dollars but printed 83.083.0 dollars. How many times larger is the printed amount?
Show the solution
In 8.308.30 the 88 sits in the ones column, and in 83.083.0 it has slid into the tens column, so it counts for ten times as much and every other digit does too. The printed amount is 1010​ times larger. Checking directly, 83.0÷8.3=1083.0÷8.3=10, which is exactly what moving the point one place right does.
Practice
An app should have multiplied 4.54.5 grams by 1010 but divided by 1010 instead, showing 0.450.45 grams. How many times larger is the correct amount, 4545 grams, than 0.450.45 grams?
Show the solution
Getting from 0.450.45 up to 4545 moves the point two places right, and each place is a factor of 1010, so the correct amount is 10×10=10010×10=100​ times larger. Dividing directly agrees, 450.45=450045=1000.4545​=454500​=100. The gap is two steps because the app divided by 1010 where it should have multiplied by 1010.
Practice
Using tiles 00, 33, 88 in the three blank slots of 0.0‾ 0‾ 0‾0.0​0​0​, build the smallest positive decimal greater than zero.
Show the solution
The tenths place counts for the most, so park the 00 there. Of the two digits left, the smaller one goes in the stronger place, so 33 in hundredths and 88 in thousandths, giving 0.0380.038​. Swapping them gives the bigger 0.0830.083, and any nonzero tile in tenths jumps you to at least 0.30.3.
